title: Classify: a checked computer-vision example
description: Prepare unchanged downloaded crops with explicit well identities, run the current computer-vision family, and inspect a deliberately small model without overstating its performance.
objectives: Find the computer-vision family inside the main Classify module.
Prepare an explicit existing split from downloaded annotations without modifying source images or labels.
Keep actual wells separate, show training figures and distinguish workflow completion from useful prediction.
Locate saved models, predictions and related nested workflows.
prerequisite: Use the Annotate lesson's Load test data download, not Stream, retaining plate1/measurements/measurements.db and its png crops. This recording uses spaCR 1.5.0.6. Download the helper ZIP and run prepare_classify_split.py in the spaCR environment with --source pointing to plate1 and --destination to a NEW folder. The helper is deliberately restricted to this four-well example: eight existing infected=1 and eight infected=2 labels per well, deterministically ranked before fitting, 64 byte-identical RGB crops. It gives copied files canonical database prcfo names; the original legacy filename parser is NOT fixed. The balanced subset does NOT preserve population prevalence. Select that prepared folder in Classify, Computer Vision (Torch), with Generate training dataset OFF. Native settings: ResNet18, epochs=1, batch_size=8, image_size=128, n_jobs=0, init_weights=False, augment=False, val_split=0.5, test_split=0.5, cv_group_by=well, random_seed=42, train_channels=['r','g','b'], train/test/plot=True; all leakage guards remain enabled. The prepared train folder has 32 crops split into 16 train and 16 validation; test has 32. Actual well sets are disjoint but share one plate. This tiny run predicts class zero for all test crops: accuracy=0.5, majority accuracy=0.5, macro F1=1/3. All 32 prediction identities, labels and probability sums, accuracy, support and macro F1 were independently checked; not every reported metric was validated. Outputs are under model/resnet18/rgb/epochs_1. API: spacr.classify.classify dispatches to spacr.deep_spacr.train_test_model. No model quality, biological validation, new-experiment generalization or submitted AI answer is claimed.

scenes.narration: Open Classify from Home and choose Computer Vision, Torch. Computer vision learns from object images; the tabular family learns from saved measurements. Both now belong to the same main module. This lesson runs a small, checked image example, with a separate preparation workaround that does not repair the application's legacy filename parser.

Follow Annotate's linked tutorial to Load the real example, keeping its measurements database and image crops. The terminal lists the existing annotation labels across four actual wells. We preserve those labels; they are not independently validated biological truth. The source project remains unchanged throughout this demonstration.

Download the helper and run it in your spaCR environment. Source is the downloaded plate folder; destination must be a new folder. It copies eight images from each of two existing classes in each well: sixty-four images total. Selection is deterministic and happens before training, not after looking at model performance.

Read the manifest before continuing. Copied filenames use the database's canonical object identities, and every image retains its original bytes. Two whole wells go into the training folder and two into test. This explicitly balanced teaching subset changes the class prevalence; it is not a representative estimate of the original population.

In Classify, choose the prepared dataset folder, not the original project or one class subfolder. It contains train and test directories, each with two class folders. The source chooser opens that existing dataset. Do not overwrite the source project or reuse a destination containing results from an earlier run.

Turn Generate training dataset off because the split is already prepared. Train and Test remain on; applying the model to a full dataset stays off. The prepared class folders preserve labels one and two, while the model uses class indices zero and one. Those numbering systems are different, not contradictory.

Choose ResNet18 for this bounded example: one epoch, batches of eight, image size one hundred twenty-eight, and zero loader workers. Use all three RGB channels and leave pretrained weights and augmentation off. These settings make the demonstration small; they are not a recommended recipe for an accurate classifier.

Keep grouping by well and every leakage check enabled. A validation fraction of one half splits the thirty-two training-folder images into sixteen training and sixteen validation images, with one whole well each. The other thirty-two images remain test-only. All four wells share one plate, so this is not an independent-experiment validation.

Turn Plot on, clear the settings search, and press Run. Watch the console for the resolved split, leakage audits, training and saved paths. Both well-grouped boundary checks pass in this recorded run. A software pass only has meaning when the names agree with the actual sample identities, which we checked separately.

The Figures panel shows loss, accuracy and per-class validation accuracy. With only one epoch, these are individual points, not evidence of convergence. Our separate test check finds every image predicted as class zero: fifty percent accuracy, exactly the balanced majority baseline. Successful execution has not produced a useful classifier.

Keep the model directory with its checkpoint, model card, leakage audits and result tables. Here it is under model, resnet18, rgb, epochs underscore one. Compare saved prediction identities and class labels, not just an accuracy number. Misclassified review images are outputs, not additional independent training or test samples.

The AI control can help you ask about settings or outputs after you configure a provider. This is an unsent question, not an answer or an analysis result. In Python, classify dispatches to train_test_model for this family. Keep the split manifest and verify advice before planning a larger, independently validated experiment.
